 Judgment
Dated this the 11th day of February 2020 S.Manikumar, CJ.

While disposing of O.P.(KAT)No.342/2018 dated 05.07.2019 the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court at paragraph No.5 ordered thus:
"5.

All vacancies (approximately five in number) existing up to the date of coming into force of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 on 5.8.2011 should be filled up by qualified Junior Health Inspectors.
The Junior Health Inspectors shall be promoted to the re-designated post of Food Safety Officer by the appointing authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The remaining substantive vacancies to the post of Food Safety Officer shall be filled up from the ranked list published by the Public Service Commission on 9.9.2016.
The impugned order of the Tribunal in so far as it relates to the petitioners shall stand modified and necessary follow up action shall be taken by the respondents forthwith."
2. Alleging wilful disobedience, instant contempt application has been filed.

3. On 6.2.2020, Mr.Tek Chand, learned Government Pleader who took notice on behalf of the respondents submitted that promotion order has already been prepared however the concerned officer was not in station to issue the order.
Con.Case(C).No.2139 OF 2019 4.

On this day, when the matter came up for further hearing, inviting attention of this Court to G.O.
(Rt)No.282/2020/H&FWD dated 10.02.2020 Mr.Teck Chand, learned Government Pleader submitted that orders of this Court have been complied with in letter and spirit and that promotion has been given to the contempt petitioners as Food Safety Officer as against the vacancies up to 05.08.2011.

A copy of the said G.O. is extracted hereunder:
"The Hon'ble High Court in the judgment read as 1st paper above has directed that all vacancies of Food Inspectors (approximately five in number) that existed up to the date of coming into force of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 on 5.8.2011 Saran G vs Dr.Rajan.N.Khobragade Ias on 11 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175661523/
2 should be filled up by qualified Junior Health Inspectors.
The Junior Health Inspectors shall be promoted to the re-designated post of Food Safety Officer by the appointing authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The remaining substantive vacancies to the post of Food Safety Officer shall be filled up from the ranked list published by the Public Service Commission on 9.9.2016.

2. As per Government order read as 2nd paper above, Government had directed Director of Health Services to prepare and furnish a proposal in respect of the qualified Junior Health Inspectors fit for promotion to the post of Food Inspectors based on their seniority and qualification in accordance with the judgment read as Ist paper above.

3. Accordingly, as per order read as 4th paper above, Director of Health Services prepared and published the finalized list of departmental candidates fit for promotion to Con.Case(C).No.2139 OF 2019 the post of Food Inspector (Re-designated as Food Safety Officer).

As per letter read as 5th paper above,
Director of Health Services has reported that as per order read as 3rd paper above Junior Health Inspectors with regular service of 5 years can be considered only in the absence of Health Inspectors.
Out of the 198 applications received there are many applicants who held the Post of Health Inspectors before 05/08/2011.

Hence the Director of Health Services has prepared the list of departmental candidates fit for promotion to the post of Food inspectors including 8 senior most candidates who were Health Inspectors before 05/08/2011 fit for promotion to the post of Food Inspector (Re-designated as Food Safety Officer), before Government.

4. Meanwhile, the Hon'ble High Court, in judgment read as 6th paper above, has ordered that out of the five vacancies, one vacancy is still remaining and that vacancy shall not be filled, until farther orders from the Court.
5.

Government have examined the matter in detail and pleased to promote the following senior most 4 candidates, from the list of departmental candidates fit for promotion to the post of Food Inspector (Re- designated as Food Safety Officer) as Food Inspectors (re-designated as Food Safety Officers) and to absorb them in Food Safety Department from the Department of Health Services, as per the existing rules.
Director of Health Services shall take necessary steps to relieve the Officers in time.
The Officers shall report before Commissioner of Food Safety immediately after relieving from Health Services Department.
The Commissioner, Food Safety shall issue suitable posting orders to the Officers, after obtaining willingness/option from the incumbents, under intimation to Government.

i) Ganesh Babu V., Health Supervisor, Community Health Con.Case(C).No.2139 OF 2019 Centre, Koduvayoor.
ii) Radhakrishnan K, Health Supervisor, Community Health Centre, Anandapuram.
Saran G vs Dr.Rajan.N.Khobragade Ias on 11 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175661523/
3 iii) Nandakumar B, Health Supervisor, Taluk Head Quarters Hospital, Nileswar.
iv) Mohandas K., Health Supervisor, Community Health Centre, Orkatteri 6.
The direction of Hon'ble High Court in the order read as Ist paper above is thus complied with."
5. Smt.Amrutha Sanjeev, learned counsel for the contempt petitioners has submitted that the orders have not been implemented in letter and spirit.
She sought for permission to ventilate the grievance of the contempt petitioners in separate proceedings, if so advised.
In as much as there is compliance of the directions issued, we do not find any wilful contempt in the contempt petition to proceed further under the Contempt of Court Act, 1971.
Accordingly, contempt petition is closed.

SD/-
S.MANIKUMAR CHIEF JUSTICE SD/-
